newsitem.title: ITALY: Malta says will continue EU dialogue at own pace.
newsitem.headline: Malta says will continue EU dialogue at own pace.

text.p: Malta's Foreign Minister George Vella told his Italian counterpart Lamberto Dini on Thursday his country wanted to find the right way to continue dialogue with the European Union, the Foreign Ministry said.
It said in a statement they discussed "the recent decisions of the Maltese government and its desire to maintain and develop relations with the EU in all sectors of mutual interest".
"The two ministers agreed on the opportunity to deepen... the most effective methods for dialogue with the EU to continue," the statement said.

Malta's Prime Minister Alfred Sant, who pledged on his election last October not to proceed with Malta's application to join the EU, told Reuters last month it did not make sense for his country to become an EU member in the near future.
But he added "of course, you never say never".

Sant said Malta would follow EU regulations at its own pace and was already having informal discussions with Brussels. He said his island state off the coast of North Africa wanted to have an industrial free trade zone with the EU.
